title: truss retro findings, version 1
description: <truss dir>/retro/findings.json: the findings the truss:retro-judge agents returned and retro/cli.ts kept, plus the recurrences retro/cli.ts recur added. A judge returns each finding as one fenced block whose info string is finding, holding one JSON object under $defs.judged; retro/cli.ts findings checks each against the measures of retro/problems.json (every evidence measure must be counted with the counted value, and every cost number must equal a cited measure), gives the kept ones an id and appends them here. Lives inside .git with the truss dir and is never committed. See adr/0051-generic-retro.md, Decisions 2, 4 and 5.

v.description: File format version. A reader treats a file with any other v as absent.

findings.description: In the order retro/cli.ts kept them.

evidence.description: One counted measure the finding rests on: a key of retro/problems.json measures and its counted value.

cost.description: What the problem cost the run, counted and never guessed. Each number is at least 0 and equals the value of a measure the evidence cites; at least one is a number.

target.description: Where the fix belongs: the truss plugin, a project's config (CLAUDE.md, .claude/), or a proposed goal for product code. retro/cli.ts sets kind to proposed-goal when the path is product code.

signature.description: JavaScript regular expressions (no flags) that would match the problem when it comes back. They become a catalog entry's patterns when the fix merges.

judged.description: What a judge returns in one fenced finding block: the counting step's finding without its id, plus an optional signature.

category.description: Any non-empty string; a category outside the checklist is kept.

title.description: One line: what went wrong. A longer one is cut to 200 characters.

fix.description: The change that stops it, in one or two sentences.

finding.description: A kept finding: the judged fields plus the id and judge retro/cli.ts adds.

id.description: F-<n>, numbered from 1 in the order retro/cli.ts kept them in this truss dir.

judge.description: The label of the judge that returned it, as the PM passed it to retro/cli.ts findings.

recurred.description: A recurrence retro/cli.ts recur added (R-31): a problem a merged fix was meant to end has come back. It keeps the catalog entry's shape, and its evidence is a file and line of the structured files the counting step reads, or of the extract's catalog hits.

recurs.description: The catalog entry whose fixedBy is not null and whose patterns hit this session.
